correctness.rationale: The arithmetic and recursive definitions agree. A length-four alternating factor is impossible because the even-index track toggles, giving parity uniqueness for length >=8. The only bispecial factors of length >=8 occur at even starts of odd-length windows. For m>=8 the interleaving lift from length m to 2m+1 is injective, surjective onto the potentially bispecial factors, and preserves all four two-sided extension possibilities because outside symbols reduce to f[t-1],f[t+m]. Exhaustive base-extension relations for lengths 7..16 are calculated from observed factor sets of lengths 7..18 certified COMPLETE by the published |F(n)|=4n theorem, so the base is an exhaustive finite mathematical proof. Only lengths 2^j-1 admit bispecials for j>=3, with exactly four missing two-sided pairs. The checked packaged standalone script confirms base table and m=8..63 lifting and MAWs through length 128; infinite scope rests on proved induction, not finite logs.

value.rationale: This resolves a natural exact invariant of a named infinite automatic word: the minimal-forbidden-factor/antidictionary complexity at every sufficiently long length, not a finite arbitrary slice. Ordinary factor complexity 4n cannot determine missing two-sided extension counts due cancellation, so the classification is strictly finer. The theorem shows sparse dyadic support and exact logarithmic accumulation of the antidictionary with a structural bispecial bijection, informing constrained factor-language descriptions.
